settings.subtitle: General Tire is Continental-owned and engineered for North American driving — Calgary potholes, BC mountain runs, and Deerfoot commuting. We stock the Altimax 365AW (all-weather), Altimax Arctic 12 (studded winter), Altimax RT45 (all-season), and Grabber H/TS60 (SUV all-season) at 111 42 Ave SW.
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend General in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
General Tire was founded in 1915 in Akron, Ohio and acquired by Continental in 1987. They benefit from Continental's German engineering pipeline while being positioned for North American value-conscious buyers.

The Altimax 365AW is the General all-weather (3PMSF) — meets Alberta's winter-tire law year-round, comparable to Bridgestone WeatherPeak or Michelin CrossClimate2 at a noticeably better price. We install it often on sedans and crossovers for Calgary drivers who want one tire all year.

For dedicated winter, the Altimax Arctic 12 is studdable — built for serious cold-Canadian conditions. For trucks and SUVs, the Grabber H/TS60 handles daily highway runs and weekend gravel.

Every General we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset as our premium-priced jobs — and we price-match local Calgary competitors. Book installation or call (403) 452-4283.
settings.cta_description: Stocked General sizes installed same-day. Price-matched against any local Calgary competitor on the same model.
settings.faq_1_q: Is General a good tire brand?
settings.faq_1_a: Yes — General Tire is owned by Continental and benefits from German engineering at a North American value price. Solid build quality, reliable warranty service, and noticeably better value than Continental-branded equivalents.
settings.faq_2_q: What's the best General tire for Calgary winters?
settings.faq_2_a: For dedicated winter, the Altimax Arctic 12 (studdable) — built for cold-Canadian conditions including Calgary's -30°C January nights. For one-tire-year-round, the Altimax 365AW — 3PMSF rated, meets Alberta winter law.
settings.faq_3_q: How much do General tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_3_a: General tires at Prince Tires range from $160 to $280 per tire. Altimax Arctic 12 starts around $165 in 15" sizes; Altimax 365AW around $190; Altimax RT45 around $250; Grabber H/TS60 around $250 for SUV sizes.
settings.faq_4_a: Yes. The Altimax 365AW carries the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) symbol — meets Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff mandate from October through April.
settings.faq_5_q: Can I get same-day General install in Calgary?
settings.faq_5_a: Yes for most stocked sizes if booked before midday. Altimax 365AW, Altimax Arctic 12, and Altimax RT45 are reliably in stock in common Calgary sizes. Grabber sizes for trucks need a 60-minute slot — call (403) 452-4283 to confirm.
settings.faq_6_q: Altimax 365AW vs Michelin CrossClimate2 — which one?
settings.faq_6_a: Both are 3PMSF-rated all-weather tires. CrossClimate2 is the premium-tier option with longer treadwear and quieter ride. Altimax 365AW uses similar technology at $80-120 less per tire. For Calgary daily commuters who want premium-adjacent at a friendlier price, the 365AW is our recommendation.
settings.calgary_richtext: Continental owns General Tire, so we sometimes pull a Grabber for trucks where Continental's own A/T price feels steep. Grabber A/TX handles Calgary's gravel-and-pavement mix; AltiMAX RT45 covers the all-season lane for sedans. Their winter Altimax Arctic 12 sees enough action in Cochrane and Airdrie commuter routes to keep us stocked through October.
settings.awards_text: Continental-owned. Same engineering pedigree as Continental at a friendlier price.
settings.testimonial_quote: Grabber A/TX on my F-150. Pulled a trailer to Bragg Creek in October — solid grip, no drone on the way back.
